evergreen_facts.text: The First Battle of Bull Run, the first major battle of the American Civil War, was fought at Manassas in 1861.
Alexandria, a port town on the Potomac River in Northern Virginia, was founded in 1749.
Arlington, Virginia, was part of the original District of Columbia until it was returned to Virginia in 1846.
Virginia's Jamestown, founded in 1607, was the first permanent English settlement in the Americas.
Mount Vernon, George Washington's plantation home, overlooks the Potomac River in Fairfax County, Virginia.
Arlington National Cemetery in Northern Virginia was established in 1864 on the grounds of Robert E. Lee's estate.
The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, headquarters of the US Department of Defense, was completed in 1943.
Dulles Airport's main terminal in Northern Virginia, designed by Eero Saarinen, opened in 1962.
Northern Virginia lies across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C., and includes Arlington and Fairfax counties.
At Great Falls Park in Northern Virginia, the Potomac River plunges through a series of jagged rocky rapids.
Shenandoah National Park protects a long stretch of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains, crossed by Skyline Drive.
Virginia is known as the "Mother of Presidents" because eight US presidents were born there.
Wolf Trap in Vienna, Virginia, is the only US national park dedicated to the performing arts.
Smithfield ham, a salt-cured and smoked country ham, is a traditional Virginia specialty.
Loudoun County in Northern Virginia is known for its many vineyards and wineries.
The Udvar-Hazy Center near Dulles in Northern Virginia displays the Space Shuttle Discovery.
